transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel worn out all the time no matter how much I rest, like I don’t have any energy left to get through work or take care of things at home. It has just gotten to the point where I'm really struggling to make it through my shifts at the store.
Along with feeling so exhausted, have you also been feeling down or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Yes, I’ve really lost that sense of ease and enjoyment in things I used to love, like gardening, fishing, and volunteering at my church. I’m just so drained and constantly worried all the time that I don't have the energy or the focus to participate in them anymore.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worry and extreme exhaustion?

It’s been going on for about a year and three months now. It really started back when my store cut my hours and my work schedule became so irregular. Ever since then, this heavy weight of worry and exhaustion just hasn't let up.
Besides feeling exhausted and worried, have you also been feeling deeply sad, down, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
No, I wouldn't say I feel deeply sad or hopeless. It's more that I feel completely drained and worn out, with my mind constantly running and consumed by worry about our finances and my family.
Along with the worry and exhaustion, do you often experience physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, or feeling constantly on edge?

Yes, I definitely feel physically tense and on edge, almost like I'm constantly waiting for something bad to happen. That tension is always there in the background making it impossible to relax, which just drains the last bit of energy I have by the time I get home.
Do you find it very difficult to control or stop these worries once they start, and do you worry about many different everyday things?

Yes, once a worry starts, it snowballs rapidly and I find it impossible to shut off, even when I try to force myself to focus on something else. I constantly worry about everyday things like paying rent, my car breaking down, my mom's health, or my hours getting cut. It quickly turns into worst-case scenarios, like worrying we'll get evicted and I won't have anything left to help my family.
Have you also been having trouble falling or staying asleep, or finding that your sleep is restless and unsatisfying?

Yes, I have a really hard time with sleep. Most nights I just lie there staring at the ceiling for an hour or two with my mind racing about bills and my work shifts. Even when I do fall asleep, I keep waking up at three or four in the morning and can't get back to sleep because I'm already worrying about the next day.
When you feel especially worried or anxious, do you experience physical reactions like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or a dry mouth?
No, I don't really experience those specific symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling when I worry. Instead, I just feel very physically tense, drained, and constantly tired.

When you feel this deep exhaustion, does it mostly get worse after activities that require mental effort, like concentrating or organizing, or does it feel more like a physical weakness that comes on after minimal physical tasks?

It honestly feels like a mix of both. I wake up already feeling exhausted because my mind is constantly running, but then simple physical things like standing at my register or cooking dinner for my family completely drain the last bit of energy I have. It just feels like both my mind and my body are constantly worn out.
Along with the exhaustion and tension, do you also frequently experience physical symptoms like tension headaches, dizziness, or an upset stomach?
I haven't really noticed those specific physical issues like headaches, dizziness, or an upset stomach. I just feel generally very tense and completely exhausted all the time.
When you are feeling very anxious or worried, do you ever experience physical sensations like shortness of breath, chest tightness, or hot flushes and cold chills?

No, I don't experience things like shortness of breath, chest tightness, or hot and cold flashes. It’s really just a constant, heavy state of physical tension and deep exhaustion that never seems to go away.
Have you noticed that you've been feeling unusually irritable or easily annoyed with others since this constant worry and exhaustion started?
I haven't really noticed feeling unusually irritable or snapping at others. I feel much more exhausted, tense, and drained rather than angry or easily annoyed.
Do you feel that your constant exhaustion is mainly a result of the ongoing worry and physical tension, or does the fatigue feel like a separate, independent problem?

I definitely feel like the exhaustion is directly tied to the constant worrying and physical tension. Lying awake at night with my mind racing about bills, combined with being constantly on edge during the day, just leaves me completely drained. It honestly feels like I’ve already worked a full shift before my actual day even starts.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent, excessive, and uncontrollable worry about multiple everyday topics (finances, family, employment) lasting for 15 months, which meets the duration criterion of at least 6 months. This worry is accompanied by significant motor tension (feeling physically tense and on edge, inability to relax) and sleep disturbances (difficulty falling and staying asleep due to racing thoughts). Although the patient reports significant fatigue, they explicitly state that this exhaustion is secondary to and directly caused by the chronic worry and physical tension, rather than being an independent primary fatigue syndrome like Neurasthenia (F48.0). Therefore, F41.1 is the most appropriate diagnosis.
